description: ANSWERS "how many votes did Rep. X miss", "how often does X vote with their party", "party unity score" -- attendance and party-line share for ONE member (House, or a senator with chamber "senate") over a session (or a roll range), computed from the U.S. House Clerk's roll-call votes or, for the Senate, the Congressional Record's printed roll calls. Nothing is returned as a bare percentage: attendance gives its denominator (recorded roll calls the member was on the roll for; quorum calls, Speaker elections and Senate rolls that could not be derived are excluded and counted; rolls before the member was seated or after they left are excluded and counted -- absence from the roll is NOT treated as Not Voting) and splits yea/nay, present and Not Voting. Party line gives two figures, each with its own denominator and exclusions: share of yea/nay votes cast with the member's party majority (a strict majority of that party's yea/nay voters; ties excluded and counted), and party unity (only the roll calls where a majority of Democrats opposed a majority of Republicans). If a figure cannot be computed from the rolls in range (member on none, no party-splitting votes, independent) it is null with a stated reason, never 0% or 100%. Independents (including the Senate's two caucusing independents) have no D-versus-R majority to compare against, so their party-line figure is null with that reason.

chamber.description: "house" (default) or "senate". The two chambers number their roll calls independently.

congress.description: Congress number, e.g. 119. Default: the newest held.

from_roll.description: First roll number of the range (default 1).

name.description: Surname as the Clerk prints it, e.g. "Pelosi"; combine with state when several members share it.

session.description: 1 or 2. Default: the newest held for the default Congress.

state.description: Two-letter state code to disambiguate a surname.

to_roll.description: Last roll number of the range (default: last roll covered).

name: member_attendance_party_line
